newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on harvest hedges, Egypt.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on harvest hedges, Egypt.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on harvest pressure including hedge selling and news that Egypt would not be in the market soon for U.S. wheat, traders said.

Only minor delays to wheat combining were reported this week in key U.S. winter wheat areas and the market was expecting Friday's USDA wheat production report to show a large production number for the U.S.
An average of analysts' estimates ahead of the report pegged 1997 U.S. winter wheat production at 1.687 billion bushels, above the output last year at 1.478 billion.
Analysts said favorable growing weather after a spring freeze in the U.S. hard red winter wheat belt is likely to prompt USDA to boost its 1997 winter wheat production forecast.
The USDA wheat production and supply/demand reports will be released Friday at 0730 CDT.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed unchanged to 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 4-1/4 cents at $3.21-1/2 a bushel. September was down 4-3/4 at $3.29-1/2.
Traders also said the market was reeling a bit from news Egypt is not seeking wheat.

Talk had circulated the markets on Wednesday that Egypt was seeking 750,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. But the Egyptian government said it had wheat stocks to last for the rest of this year and saw no immediate need to enter the wheat market.

Futures were underpinned by USDA's weekly export sales report. USDA Thursday said net export sales of U.S. wheat during the week ended July 3 totalled 735,100 tonnes, above expectations for 450,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Smith Barney, E.D. and F. Man Interntional and Merrill Lynch Futures each sold one million bushels of September, traders said. LIT America bought five million bushels of September, traders said.
In spread trading, O'Connor and Co did 1.2 million bushels of September/July at 8-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, below the 30,516 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, Term Commodities sold 200 September $3.30 calls at 11-1/2 cents and Lee B. Stern and Co sold 100 September $3.50 calls at 4-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000 contracts, below the 6,903 traded Wednesday.
